claims.text: The proposed alloy is a Ti–Ni-primary composition exemplified as Ti30Ni30Cr10Al10V10.
The initial homogenized alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
A treatment at approximately 700 °C for 2 hours followed by rapid quenching will induce precipitation.
The aging treatment will form nanoscale Ni3Ti-like precipitates in the matrix.
The Ni3Ti-like precipitates will be uniformly distributed.
The Ni3Ti-like precipitates will be coherent with the matrix.
Coherent precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitates will restrict grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Ti and Ni have an intrinsic affinity in the proposed alloy that favors the stated precipitation-strengthening mechanism.
The aged alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the untreated baseline.
The aged alloy will have better elevated-temperature creep resistance than the untreated baseline.
Load bearing and dispersion strengthening by the Ni3Ti-like precipitates will produce the predicted mechanical-property improvements.
The untreated baseline lacks controlled nanoprecipitate formation.
Aging near 700 °C for 2 hours provides favorable precipitate formation without excessive coarsening.
Deviating from the proposed aging conditions may negate the strengthening benefit.
Prolonged service-temperature exposure may coarsen the Ni3Ti-like precipitates and reduce their strengthening effect.
Mechanical testing is to be conducted above 700 °C, including creep testing at approximately 800 °C.

contradictions.description: The explicit example Ti30Ni30Cr10Al10V10 totals only 90 at%, so it is not a complete normalized composition even though the other fields present it as an alloy composition satisfying the HEA compositional definition.
The baseline is described simultaneously as 'as-cast' and 'homogenized.' Literal as-cast material has not undergone a post-casting homogenization treatment, so the processing state is ambiguous.
